display.title: Episode 553: The King Saved by a Shabbos Candle, Chapter 2 (Chanukah)
display.summary_short: A Chanukah show with favorite Chanukah songs in Hebrew, English and Yiddish, Shema with a guest from Australia, the end of the Shabbos-candle story, and what the word 'mitzvah' really means.
display.summary_long: Broadcast during Chanukah 5753. Uncle Yossi wishes everyone a happy Chanukah: the menorah's flames remind us of Hashem's miracles then and now, and we pray for Moshiach and the menorah of the Beis HaMikdash. A young studio guest sings favorite Chanukah songs: Maoz Tzur, 'I Have a Little Dreidel', a Hebrew Chanukah song and an old Yiddish one for grandparents. A boy visiting from Australia leads the Shema, followed by tzedakah and Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery. Story time concludes the tale of the king who banned candles: lost in a blizzard after his horse throws him, the king sees the light of Shabbos candles in a cabin outside the city, is welcomed to a Shabbos table, and cancels his decree. In the mailbox, a listener asks what 'mitzvah' means. Uncle Yossi explains that it means a commandment from Hashem, our Commander-in-Chief, and that this is the very point of Chanukah: the Greeks did not mind good deeds, but the Chashmonaim fought so that Jews could keep the Torah as Hashem's commands.
display.lesson: A mitzvah is a commandment from Hashem, done because He commanded it; and the light of Shabbos and Chanukah candles brings blessing and protection.
